family: C major (every tonal sound key-fitted to the white keys); ElevenLabs mallets, kalimba, glockenspiel, harp, bubbles and real-sounding parrot calls, earshot-bank wood / glock / shimmer; never a falling or buzzing cue
format: OGG Vorbis q4, 48 kHz; stereo for the rewards (side narrowed to 0.8 + a computed room), mono for UI ticks and Foni

levels.reference: his voice clips measure about -15 LUFS integrated

chain: key fit (resample, <= 1.5 semitones), high-pass 110-400 Hz, low-pass 7-14 kHz, tanh saturation 10-25 % (warmth), computed stereo room 0.25-1.2 s at 4-12 % wet, trim (onset -1 ms, -60 dB tail), fades, tier gain with a 4 dB look-ahead limiter

shipped_from: v2/almost_b.mp3) a fourth lower and slower
v2/pop_c.mp3) + earshot bank shimmer/m3 as the confetti

sounds.name: tap_1
sounds.provenance: ElevenLabs: 'A single tiny soft bop of pressing a squishy rubber toy button, mid-pitched and round like a little bubble' (v2/tap_c.mp3), a major third up
sounds.why: 'a mouth pop' 4.0, 'a liquid bloop' 3.9, 'a water drop' 3.5, p 0.99 vs harsh/buzzy; body at 750 Hz (a phone plays it); tap_a/tap_d were kicks at 105-120 Hz, tap_b 'a can opening'

sounds.name: tap_2
sounds.provenance: same tap, a step up (re-landed on a white key)
sounds.why: round-robin variant

sounds.name: tap_3
sounds.provenance: same tap, a step down (re-landed on a white key)
sounds.why: round-robin variant

sounds.name: card
sounds.provenance: ElevenLabs (v1): 'a single page of a children's picture book being turned quickly' (el7_page_turn.mp3)
sounds.why: 'a quick swipe' z 3.5, 'a soft quick paper swipe' z 4.0; all 6 v2 whoosh generations read as hits, hiss or 'error buzz'

sounds.name: nav_forward
sounds.provenance: ElevenLabs: 'Soft low gentle whoosh sliding back...' (v2/navback_a.mp3), a major third up
sounds.why: the back whoosh ('a fast whoosh' 4.5, 'a short swish' 3.7, p 1.00) raised 400 cents so forward is brighter and quicker: one pair; page_a read as 'a record scratch' 3.5 once processed (p 0.02)

sounds.name: nav_back
sounds.provenance: ElevenLabs: 'Soft low gentle whoosh sliding back...' (v2/navback_a.mp3)
sounds.why: 'a fast whoosh' 3.2, darker (518 Hz) than forward, so back sounds softer

sounds.name: mic_open
sounds.provenance: ElevenLabs: 'Tiny bright upward bloop notification... rising water-drop blip' (v2/mic_b.mp3)
sounds.why: 'bubbles underwater' 3.6 / 'a liquid bloop' 3.0, z 3.4 for 'a short cute bubbly blip'; mic_a read 'ice cubes in a glass'; trimmed to 140 ms

sounds.name: good
sounds.provenance: ElevenLabs: 'Rewarding success jingle... three fast ascending soft mallet notes on a wooden marimba with a glittering glockenspiel and magic sparkle tail' (v2/good_c.mp3) + computed soft thump
sounds.why: good_c z 3.3 (p 1.00 vs error/alarm/sad/cheap), 'kalimba' + 'glockenspiel run' tags, brightest of three (1707 Hz); good_a 3.0, good_b 2.2
sounds.earshot_query: a bright happy marimba arpeggio with a sparkling chime

sounds.name: almost
sounds.provenance: ElevenLabs: 'Soft hopeful nearly! cue... two quick bouncy kalimba notes going up, plush' (v2/almost_b.mp3)
sounds.why: z 3.7, 'a kalimba note' 3.9, p 1.00 vs sad/buzz; almost_a 2.2 read as a snare

sounds.name: retake
sounds.provenance: ElevenLabs: the 'almost' kalimba motif (v2/almost_b.mp3) a fourth lower and slower
sounds.why: the same two rising kalimba notes, lower and slower: one family, never a failure; all four retake generations had a low partial read as 'error buzz' (retake_a/c) or read as a triangle / box lid (b/d)

sounds.name: hold_tick
sounds.provenance: earshot bank: mallet/glock --pitch C6 (played at 6 rates C D E G A C')
sounds.why: 'a glass ting' 3.3, tuned C6 exactly

sounds.name: pop
sounds.provenance: ElevenLabs: 'Single satisfying bubbly pop... plump water-bubble bloop' (v2/pop_c.mp3) + earshot bank shimmer/m3 as the confetti
sounds.why: pop_c z 5.2 ('a mouth pop' 4.1, 'a bubble pop' 3.8): the strongest reading of the whole audition; pop_b read as a kick drum

sounds.name: star
sounds.provenance: ElevenLabs: 'Collecting a magic star... a soft rising harp glissando that lands on a warm round bell chime' (v2/star_c.mp3)
sounds.why: 'a glockenspiel run' 2.7, p 1.00 vs bad alts; the other three stars read mainly as a triangle; low-passed 10 kHz

sounds.name: levelup
sounds.provenance: ElevenLabs: 'Kids game level complete sparkle: quick ascending glockenspiel and celesta run that blooms into a shimmering wind-chime and bell chord' (v2/levelup_b.mp3)
sounds.why: 'a success chime' 3.1, 'a magic sparkle chime' 2.9, p 1.00; levelup_a darker, read as 'glass harp'
sounds.earshot_query: a rising magical harp glissando with chimes

sounds.name: session_end
sounds.provenance: ElevenLabs: 'Short proud celebratory fanfare... marimba and glockenspiel melody rising C, E, G, high C over a soft lush string pad' (v2/end_a.mp3)
sounds.why: already in C (C5 E6 C6 D6), 'a kalimba note' 3.3 / 'a glockenspiel run' 2.5, p 0.93; end_b had an Ab, end_c read as 'a doorbell'
sounds.earshot_query: a joyful short orchestral fanfare with mallets and strings

sounds.name: unlock
sounds.provenance: ElevenLabs: 'Magical unlock sound in a kids game: a small soft wooden latch click followed by a sparkling rising chime' (v2/unlock_a.mp3)
sounds.why: z 3.5 for 'a magical unlock chime', p 1.00; very bright (5.8 kHz) so low-passed at 9 kHz

sounds.name: mirror_match

sounds.why: 'a success chime' 4.3, 'a magic sparkle chime' 3.6, z 2.5, p 1.00; the 4 ElevenLabs shimmers read as a triangle at 7-10 kHz
